source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח קֹ֔רַח בֶּן־יִצְהָ֥ר בֶּן־קְהָ֖ת בֶּן־לֵוִ֑י וְדָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם בְּנֵ֧י אֱלִיאָ֛ב וְא֥וֹן בֶּן־פֶּ֖לֶת בְּנֵ֥י רְאוּבֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben,

en.L: And Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took [men], and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben,
en.B: Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, gathered men to his side, together with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, who were Reubenites,
en.R: Korah was the son of Izhar and a descendant of Kohath and Levi. He gathered men to stand with him. With him were Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth. These three were from the tribe of Reuben.

decisions.choice: took: the verb has no object; Korah gathered men, or took action
alternatives: became proud (a proposed correction of the text)
decisions.reason: The verb "took" normally needs an object, and none is stated. The sentence most likely means that Korah took men with him, the 250 leaders named in verse 2, or, more loosely, that he took it upon himself to act. Some have suggested that the letters were miscopied from a word meaning "became proud", but no Hebrew manuscript reads so. The sense of the story is clear either way: Korah led a revolt.

decisions.choice: Korah: a Levite of the clan of Kohath, cousin of Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Izhar was a brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Exodus 6:18-21), so Korah was their first cousin. The Kohathites carried the most holy things of the tabernacle but were not allowed to touch or see them (4:4-20). Only Aaron and his sons were priests (3:10).

decisions.choice: Dathan, Abiram and On: leaders from Reuben, the tribe of Jacob's firstborn
decisions.reason: Reuben was Jacob's firstborn son (Genesis 49:3), and his tribe may have resented its loss of first place. Eliab was a grandson of Reuben (26:5-9). On is not mentioned again in the story; the record leaves his fate unstated. Reuben and the Kohathites both camped on the south side of the tabernacle (2:10; 3:29), so the rebels were neighbors.

decisions.choice: took [men] / gathered men to his side / gathered men to stand with him
decisions.reason: English cannot leave "took" without an object, so all levels supply the most likely one, men, following meaning decision m1. Literal brackets it.

source.text: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים מִבְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם נְשִׂיאֵ֥י עֵדָ֛ה קְרִאֵ֥י מוֹעֵ֖ד אַנְשֵׁי־שֵֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: and they rose up before Moses, and men from [the] sons of Israel, fifty and two hundred, leaders of [the] congregation, called [ones] of [the] assembly, men of name.

en.L: and they rose up before Moses, and men from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 250, leaders of the congregation, called [ones] of the assembly, men of name.
en.B: and they rose up against Moses. With them were 250 men from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, leaders of the congregation, chosen members of the council, men of renown.
en.R: They rose up against Moses, and 250 men from among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} joined them. These men were leaders of the community. They had been chosen to sit in the council, and everyone knew who they were.

decisions.choice: rose up before Moses: stood up to oppose him
decisions.reason: To "rise up before" someone can mean to stand in respect, but here, with the complaint of verse 3, it means to confront and challenge him.

decisions.choice: called of the assembly: men summoned to the council
decisions.reason: The phrase describes men regularly called to the gathering where the people's affairs were decided. A similar title is used of the leaders in 1:16 and 26:9. These were not ordinary members of the community but its recognized leaders.

decisions.choice: men of name: well-known, respected men
decisions.reason: A "name" is a reputation (Genesis 6:4). The rebellion was led by men of standing, which made it more serious.

decisions.choice: chosen members of the council / chosen to sit in the council
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the title means instead of giving the bare "called ones of the meeting" that Literal keeps.

source.text: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵהֶם֮ רַב־לָכֶם֒ כִּ֤י כָל־הָֽעֵדָה֙ כֻּלָּ֣ם קְדֹשִׁ֔ים וּבְתוֹכָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וּמַדּ֥וּעַ תִּֽתְנַשְּׂא֖וּ עַל־קְהַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they assembled against Moses and against Aaron, and they said to them, Much for you! For all the congregation, all of them [are] holy, and in their midst [is] Yahweh. And why do you lift yourselves up over [the] assembly of Yahweh?

en.L: And they assembled against Moses and against Aaron and said to them, "Too much for you! For all the congregation, all of them [are] holy, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] in their midst. And why do you lift yourselves up over the assembly of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.B: They came together against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You claim too much! Every member of the congregation is holy, all of them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is among them. What right have you to raise yourselves above the assembly of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?"
en.R: They gathered as a group against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You are taking too much on yourselves! Everyone in the community is holy, every one of them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is among them. So why do you put yourselves above {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s assembly?"

decisions.choice: much for you: you have taken too much on yourselves
decisions.reason: The two words say "much to you": you have more than your share, you go too far. Moses throws the same words back at the Levites in verse 7.

decisions.choice: all the congregation is holy: a true belief used for a false claim
decisions.reason: God had called all Israel "a holy nation" (Exodus 19:6) and had just told them to be holy to their God (15:40). The rebels use this to deny that Moses and Aaron have any special place. The story answers that holiness is God's to give, and that he chooses who may come near (verses 5 and 7).

decisions.choice: lift yourselves up: claim a higher rank
decisions.reason: The verb means to raise oneself, to act as a superior. The rebels accuse Moses and Aaron of making themselves rulers, though the LORD appointed them.

decisions.choice: You claim too much / You are taking too much on yourselves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the short protest; Literal keeps its bare form. The same English is used in verse 7, where Moses answers with the same words.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיִּפֹּ֖ל עַל־פָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Moses, and he fell on his face.

en.L: And Moses heard [it] and fell on his face.
en.B: When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.
en.R: When Moses heard this, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: fell on his face: a gesture of humility and of appeal to God
decisions.reason: Moses does not answer at once but throws himself down, as he and Aaron did when the people rebelled in 14:5. The gesture appears again in verse 22, where it goes with prayer.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־קֹ֜רַח וְאֶֽל־כָּל־עֲדָתוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בֹּ֠קֶר וְיֹדַ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וְאֶת־הַקָּד֖וֹשׁ וְהִקְרִ֣יב אֵלָ֑יו וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַר־בּ֖וֹ יַקְרִ֥יב אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to Korah and to all his company, saying, Morning, and will make known Yahweh who [is] his, and the holy [one], and he will bring [him] near to himself; and whom he will choose, he will bring near to himself.

en.L: And he spoke to Korah and to all his company, saying, "[In the] morning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will make known who [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, and the holy [one], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring [him] near to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; and the one whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring near to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.B: Then he said to Korah and all his company, "In the morning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will show who belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and who is holy, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will let that man come near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring near to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: He said to Korah and all his followers, "In the morning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will show who belongs to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and who is holy. He will let that man come near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will bring near the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

decisions.choice: his company: Korah's band of followers
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the whole congregation of Israel (verse 3). Used of Korah and his followers, it marks them as a rival congregation.

decisions.choice: bring near: let someone approach God as a priest
decisions.reason: To "come near" or be "brought near" to the LORD is the language of priestly service at the altar and in the tabernacle (3:10; Leviticus 10:3). Whoever else came near was to die (1:51; 3:10). The question is not who is holy in general but who may serve as priest.

decisions.choice: whom he will choose: holiness and priesthood are the LORD's choice
decisions.reason: Moses puts the decision in God's hands. The answer comes in verse 35 and again with Aaron's staff in 17:16-28.

decisions.choice: company / followers
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "company" for Korah's group, keeping "congregation" for Israel as a whole; Readable says "followers". Meaning decision m1 notes that the Hebrew word is the same.

source.text: זֹ֖את עֲשׂ֑וּ קְחוּ־לָכֶ֣ם מַחְתּ֔וֹת קֹ֖רַח וְכָל־עֲדָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: This do: take for yourselves censers, Korah and all his company,

en.L: Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all his company,
en.B: Do this, Korah, you and all your company: take censers,
en.R: Here is what you must do, Korah, you and all your followers. Take fire pans for burning incense.

decisions.choice: censers: pans for carrying burning coals
decisions.reason: The word names a metal pan or scoop used to carry hot coals, on which incense was burned (Leviticus 10:1; 16:12). Offering incense was a priest's task (Exodus 30:7-8).

decisions.choice: you and all your company
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his company" while speaking to Korah. Balanced and Readable say "your", since Korah is addressed.

decisions.choice: fire pans for burning incense
decisions.reason: Readable describes the object, since "censer" is not a common word.

source.text: וּתְנ֣וּ בָהֵ֣ן׀אֵ֡שׁ וְשִׂימוּ֩ עֲלֵיהֶ֨ן קְטֹ֜רֶת לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ מָחָ֔ר וְהָיָ֗ה הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הַקָּד֑וֹשׁ רַב־לָכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: and put in them fire, and set on them incense before Yahweh tomorrow; and it will be [that] the man whom chooses Yahweh, he [is] the holy [one]. Much for you, sons of Levi!

en.L: and put fire in them and set incense on them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tomorrow. And it will be [that] the man whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chooses, he [is] the holy [one]. Too much for you, sons of Levi!"
en.B: and tomorrow put fire in them and lay incense on them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The man {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you Levites who claim too much!"
en.R: Tomorrow put hot coals in them and put incense on the coals in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The man {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chooses is the one who is holy. You Levites are the ones taking too much on yourselves!"

decisions.choice: put fire in them and incense on them: the act that killed Nadab and Abihu
decisions.reason: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire and incense in them, and offered fire the LORD had not commanded; fire came from the LORD and consumed them (Leviticus 10:1-2; Numbers 3:4). The test Moses proposes is dangerous, and the reader knows it.

decisions.choice: much for you, sons of Levi: Moses turns the rebels' words back on them
decisions.reason: The rebels said "much for you" to Moses and Aaron (verse 3); Moses now says it to the Levites with Korah. They, not he, are the ones claiming too much.

decisions.choice: hot coals
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "fire" in a censer was: burning coals.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־קֹ֑רַח שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֖א בְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Korah, Hear, please, sons of Levi!

en.L: And Moses said to Korah, "Hear, please, sons of Levi!
en.B: Moses also said to Korah, "Listen, you Levites!
en.R: Then Moses said to Korah, "Listen to me, you Levites!

decisions.choice: to Korah ... sons of Levi: Korah addressed as head of the Levites with him
decisions.reason: Moses speaks to Korah but addresses the Levites who side with him. Verses 8-11 deal with the Levites' claim to the priesthood; Dathan and Abiram's complaint is answered separately (verses 12-15).

source.text: הַמְעַ֣ט מִכֶּ֗ם כִּֽי־הִבְדִּיל֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַקְרִ֥יב אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָ֑יו לַעֲבֹ֗ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַת֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְלַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדָ֖ה לְשָׁרְתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] too little for you that has set apart [the] God of Israel you from [the] congregation of Israel to bring near you to himself, to serve [the] service of [the] tabernacle of Yahweh, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?

en.L: [Is it] too little for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the congregation of Israel to bring you near to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, to do the service of the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
en.B: Does it mean so little to you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the congregation of Israel, bringing you near to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to do the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle and to stand before the congregation and serve them?
en.R: The God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the Israelite community. He has brought you close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to do the work at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle and to serve the people. Is that not enough for you?

decisions.choice: set you apart: the Levites' separation for the LORD
decisions.reason: The same verb describes the setting apart of the Levites in 8:14: they belong to the LORD in place of Israel's firstborn (3:12-13; 8:16-18).

decisions.choice: the service of the tabernacle ... to minister to them: the Levites' duties
decisions.reason: The Levites guarded and carried the tabernacle and helped the priests (1:50-53; 3:5-9; chapter 4). In doing so they served the whole community, standing between the people and the holy things so that wrath would not fall on Israel (1:53).

decisions.choice: is it too little for you?: a reproach
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no, it is a great honor" and rebukes the Levites for wanting more. Dathan and Abiram use the same opening in verse 13.

decisions.choice: statement first, question last
decisions.reason: Readable states the Levites' privileges first and puts the short question at the end, so the long sentence is easier to follow. It also supplies "the rest of", implied by "set apart from".

source.text: וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְאֶת־כָּל־אַחֶ֥יךָ בְנֵי־לֵוִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֖ם גַּם־כְּהֻנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and he has brought near you and all your brothers, [the] sons of Levi, with you, and you seek also priesthood?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought you near, and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you; and would you seek the priesthood too?
en.B: He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you want the priesthood as well?
en.R: He has brought you and all the other Levites close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And now you want to be priests as well!

decisions.choice: priesthood: the office given only to Aaron and his sons
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the priesthood to Aaron and his descendants (Exodus 28:1; Numbers 3:10; 18:7). Korah, a Levite but not a son of Aaron, wanted it for himself and those with him.

decisions.choice: you (singular) ... you seek (plural): Korah and the Levites together
decisions.reason: "You" is singular when God brings Korah near and plural when Moses asks whether they seek the priesthood. Korah is addressed as the leader, with all the Levites who side with him.

decisions.choice: want to be priests
decisions.reason: Readable says what seeking the priesthood means.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־עֲדָ֣תְךָ֔ הַנֹּעָדִ֖ים עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן מַה־ה֔וּא כִּ֥י תַלִּ֖ינוּ עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore you and all your company [are] the ones gathered against Yahweh; and Aaron, what [is] he, that you grumble against him?

en.L: Therefore you and all your company [are] those gathered together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And Aaron, what [is] he, that you grumble against him?"
en.B: So it is against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that you and all your company have banded together. Who is Aaron, that you grumble against him?"
en.R: So it is really {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that you and all your followers are against. Who is Aaron, that you complain about him?"

decisions.choice: gathered against the LORD: rebellion against the one who appointed Aaron
decisions.reason: Since the LORD chose Aaron, an attack on Aaron is an attack on the LORD. Moses said the same of the people's grumbling about food (Exodus 16:7-8).

decisions.choice: you grumble: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two forms of the same verb "grumble". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: grumble: the word for Israel's complaints in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Israel's grumbling against Moses and Aaron (Exodus 16:2, 7; Numbers 14:2, 27, 29) and returns in 17:6, 20.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֹשֶׁ֔ה לִקְרֹ֛א לְדָתָ֥ן וְלַאֲבִירָ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיאָ֑ב וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַעֲלֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Moses to call Dathan and Abiram, [the] sons of Eliab, and they said, Not we will come up!

en.L: And Moses sent to summon Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and they said, "We will not come up!
en.B: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, "We will not come up!
en.R: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they answered, "We will not come!

decisions.choice: come up: appear before a leader or court
decisions.reason: "Going up" is used for coming before a ruler or a court to be heard (Genesis 46:31; Deuteronomy 25:7; Judges 4:5). Dathan and Abiram refuse to recognize Moses' authority. Their refusal opens and closes their reply (verse 14).

decisions.choice: come
decisions.reason: Readable drops "up", which carries the idiom of appearing before a judge; Literal and Balanced keep it.

source.text: הַמְעַ֗ט כִּ֤י הֶֽעֱלִיתָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־תִשְׂתָּרֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ גַּם־הִשְׂתָּרֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] too little that you have brought us up from a land flowing [with] milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you lord it over us, also lording it?

en.L: [Is it] too little that you have brought us up out of a land flowing [with] milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, that you must also lord it over us, indeed lord it?
en.B: Was it a small thing to bring us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey only to kill us in the wilderness? Must you now also lord it over us, and lord it completely?
en.R: You took us away from a land flowing with milk and honey, and you brought us out here to kill us in the desert. Is that not enough? Now you also want to rule over us completely!

decisions.choice: a land flowing with milk and honey: said of Egypt
decisions.reason: This is the LORD's own description of the promised land (Exodus 3:8; Numbers 13:27; 14:8). Dathan and Abiram turn it around and use it of Egypt, the land of slavery, as the people did in 11:5 and 14:3-4.

decisions.choice: lord it over us, also lording it: an emphatic repetition
decisions.reason: The verb, "to make oneself a prince", is repeated with emphasis: you want to be our absolute ruler. It is the charge of verse 3 in harsher words.

decisions.choice: is it too little?: the same question Moses asked
decisions.reason: Dathan and Abiram begin with the words Moses used to the Levites in verse 9.

decisions.choice: statement first, question after
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Readable gives the complaint first and puts the short question after it.

source.text: אַ֡ף לֹ֣א אֶל־אֶרֶץ֩ זָבַ֨ת חָלָ֤ב וּדְבַשׁ֙ הֲבִ֣יאֹתָ֔נוּ וַתִּ֨תֶּן־לָ֔נוּ נַחֲלַ֖ת שָׂדֶ֣ה וָכָ֑רֶם הַעֵינֵ֞י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָהֵ֛ם תְּנַקֵּ֖ר לֹ֥א נַעֲלֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Moreover, not into a land flowing [with] milk and honey have you brought us, and [not] given to us an inheritance of field and vineyard. [The] eyes of those men will you gouge out? Not we will come up!

en.L: Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing [with] milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of field and vineyard. Will you gouge out the eyes of those men? We will not come up!"
en.B: Besides, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us fields and vineyards to own. Do you mean to gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up!"
en.R: You have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey. You have not given us any fields or vineyards of our own. Do you think you can blind these men to what you are doing? We will not come!"

decisions.choice: gouge out the eyes of those men: blind them, deceive them
alternatives: a sneer at a threat of physical blinding
decisions.reason: Most likely the question means "Do you think you can blind us to the truth?": Moses cannot hide from the people that he has failed to bring them into the land. "Those men" probably means the speakers themselves, said indirectly. It could also be a sneer at a threat of real punishment, since putting out eyes was done to captives (Judges 16:21; 1 Samuel 11:2).

decisions.choice: an inheritance of field and vineyard: the land promised but not yet given
decisions.reason: The people would not enter the land because of their refusal in chapter 14 (14:22-23, 29-30). Dathan and Abiram blame Moses for it.

decisions.choice: blind these men to what you are doing
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the picture, following meaning decision m1; Literal and Balanced keep "gouge out the eyes".

source.text: וַיִּ֤חַר לְמֹשֶׁה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה אַל־תֵּ֖פֶן אֶל־מִנְחָתָ֑ם לֹ֠א חֲמ֨וֹר אֶחָ֤ד מֵהֶם֙ נָשָׂ֔אתִי וְלֹ֥א הֲרֵעֹ֖תִי אֶת־אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it burned to Moses greatly, and he said to Yahweh, Do not turn to their offering! Not one donkey from them have I taken, and not have I harmed one of them.

en.L: And Moses burned [with anger] greatly, and he said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Do not turn to their offering. Not one donkey have I taken from them, and I have not harmed one of them."
en.B: Moses was furious, and he said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Pay no regard to their offering. I have not taken so much as one donkey from them, and I have done none of them any wrong."
en.R: Moses became very angry. He said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Do not accept their offering. I have never taken even one donkey from them. I have never done anything wrong to any of them."

decisions.choice: do not turn to their offering: do not accept it
decisions.reason: To "turn to" an offering is to look on it with favor and accept it. The word for offering can mean any gift brought to God, not only the grain offering; here it is the incense the rebels will bring tomorrow (verses 16-17).

decisions.choice: not one donkey: Moses has never abused his position
decisions.reason: A ruler could seize his people's animals and goods (1 Samuel 8:16). Moses denies any such abuse, answering the charge that he lords it over them (verse 13). Samuel makes the same defense in 1 Samuel 12:3.

decisions.choice: burned [with anger]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "it burned to Moses", an idiom for anger; Literal brackets "with anger".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־קֹ֔רַח אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־עֲדָ֣תְךָ֔ הֱי֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אַתָּ֥ה וָהֵ֛ם וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן מָחָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Korah, You and all your company, be before Yahweh, you and they and Aaron, tomorrow.

en.L: And Moses said to Korah, "You and all your company, be before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you and they and Aaron, tomorrow.
en.B: Moses said to Korah, "Tomorrow you and all your company must appear before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: you, they, and Aaron.
en.R: Then Moses said to Korah, "Tomorrow you and all your followers must come and stand in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You, your followers, and Aaron must all be there.

decisions.choice: be before the LORD: appear at the tent of meeting
decisions.reason: To be "before the LORD" is to come to his dwelling, here the entrance of the tent of meeting (verse 18).

source.text: וּקְח֣וּ׀אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קְטֹ֔רֶת וְהִקְרַבְתֶּ֞ם לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֔וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמָאתַ֖יִם מַחְתֹּ֑ת וְאַתָּ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן אִ֥ישׁ מַחְתָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And take each his censer, and put on them incense, and bring near before Yahweh each his censer, fifty and two hundred censers; and you and Aaron each his censer.

en.L: And take each man his censer, and put incense on them, and bring near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} each man his censer, 250 censers; and you and Aaron, each his censer."
en.B: Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it, and each is to bring his censer before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, 250 censers. You and Aaron are also to bring your censers."
en.R: Each man must take his fire pan and put incense in it. Then all 250 men will bring their fire pans to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You and Aaron must also bring your fire pans."

decisions.choice: bring near: the priestly word again
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verses 5 and 9-10 for coming near to God. The rebels are to do what they claim the right to do, and the LORD will show whether he accepts it.

decisions.choice: fire pans
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֵ֔שׁ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְטֹ֑רֶת וַֽיַּעַמְד֗וּ פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וּמֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took each his censer, and they put on them fire, and they set on them incense, and they stood [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting, and Moses and Aaron.

en.L: And they took each man his censer, and they put fire in them and laid incense on them, and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and Moses and Aaron [too].
en.B: So each man took his censer, put fire in it, and laid incense on it. Then they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
en.R: So each man took his fire pan, put hot coals in it, and put incense on the coals. They stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: and Moses and Aaron: the two sides stand together at the tent
decisions.reason: Moses and Aaron are added at the end of the sentence: they too took their places at the entrance, as verses 16-17 required, ready for the LORD to decide between them and the rebels.

source.text: וַיַּקְהֵ֨ל עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם קֹ֨רַח֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיֵּרָ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־כָּל־הָעֵדָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And assembled against them Korah all the congregation to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting; and appeared [the] glory of Yahweh to all the congregation.

en.L: And Korah assembled all the congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to all the congregation.
en.B: Korah gathered the whole congregation against Moses and Aaron at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to the whole congregation.
en.R: Korah got the whole community to gather against Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the meeting tent. Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to everyone there.

decisions.choice: against them: against Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to Moses and Aaron, just named in verse 18. Korah has won the whole congregation to his side.

decisions.choice: the glory of the LORD: the visible sign of the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The LORD's glory appeared at the tent in a moment of crisis, as when the people wanted to stone Joshua and Caleb (14:10) and when they grumbled for food (Exodus 16:10). Each time it comes before judgment.

decisions.choice: against Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two men "them" refers to, following meaning decision m1.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: introduces the LORD's words
decisions.reason: The usual formula introducing what the LORD says, here to Moses and Aaron together.

source.text: הִבָּ֣דְל֔וּ מִתּ֖וֹךְ הָעֵדָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את וַאַכַלֶּ֥האֹתָ֖ם כְּרָֽגַע׃

records.literal_gloss: Separate yourselves from [the] midst of this congregation, and I will consume them in a moment.

en.L: "Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them in a moment."
en.B: "Get away from this congregation, so that I can destroy them in an instant."
en.R: "Move away from these people, so that I can destroy them right now."

decisions.choice: consume: bring to an end, destroy completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to finish or bring to an end. The LORD said the same of the people after the golden calf (Exodus 32:10) and threatened them again after their refusal to enter the land (14:12).

decisions.choice: this congregation: the whole people gathered by Korah
decisions.reason: The threat is against the congregation that Korah assembled (verse 19), not only the leaders of the revolt. Moses and Aaron's prayer in verse 22 asks the LORD to spare them.

decisions.choice: these people
decisions.reason: Readable says "these people" for "this congregation", the whole crowd gathered at the tent.

source.text: וַיִּפְּל֤וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶם֙ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֕ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָרוּחֹ֖ת לְכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר הָאִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ יֶחֱטָ֔א וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הָעֵדָ֖ה תִּקְצֹֽף׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they fell on their faces, and they said, God, God of the spirits of all flesh, the one man sins, and against all the congregation will you be angry?

en.L: And they fell on their faces and said, "God, God of the spirits of all flesh, one man sins, and will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be angry with all the congregation?"
en.B: But they fell facedown and said, "God, God of the spirits of all humankind, when one man sins, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be angry with the whole congregation?"
en.R: But Moses and Aaron bowed down with their faces to the ground. They said, "God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give life and breath to every person. When only one man has sinned, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be angry with the whole community?"

decisions.choice: God of the spirits of all flesh: the God who gives every human being life
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means living humankind and "spirit" the breath of life God gives (Genesis 2:7; 6:17). As the giver of every life, God knows each person and can tell the guilty from the innocent. Moses uses the title again in 27:16.

decisions.choice: one man sins, and will you be angry with all?: a plea for justice
decisions.reason: The question asks God not to punish all for the sin of one. The "one man" is Korah, who led the congregation (verse 19). Compare Abraham's plea for Sodom (Genesis 18:23-25).

decisions.choice: all humankind
decisions.reason: Balanced says "all humankind" for "all flesh", since here the phrase means human beings. Literal keeps "flesh".

decisions.choice: you give life and breath to every person
decisions.reason: Readable turns the title into a statement of what it means. It also names Moses and Aaron as "they".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: introduces the LORD's answer
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. The LORD answers the prayer of verse 22 by sparing the congregation if it moves away from the rebels.

decisions.choice: answered
decisions.reason: Readable says "answered", since this is the reply to the prayer of verse 22.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־הָעֵדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵֽעָלוּ֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב לְמִשְׁכַּן־קֹ֖רַח דָּתָ֥ן וַאֲבִירָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to the congregation, saying, Get yourselves up from round about [the] dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.

en.L: "Speak to the congregation, saying, 'Get yourselves up from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'"
en.B: "Tell the congregation, 'Move away from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'"
en.R: "Tell the community to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."

decisions.choice: dwelling: the rebels' tents
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the LORD's dwelling, the tabernacle, but here it means the rebels' living quarters, their tents (verse 27). Set beside the LORD's tabernacle, it may hint at a rival sanctuary. It is singular, perhaps for the area where the three lived, since Kohathites and Reubenites camped on the same south side (2:10; 3:29).

decisions.choice: get yourselves up from: withdraw from
decisions.reason: The verb means to go up, here to move away from a place. It is the same verb the rebels used when they refused to "come up" (verses 12, 14).

decisions.choice: dwellings / tents
decisions.reason: Balanced says "dwellings" in the plural, since each man had his own tent (verse 27); Readable says "tents".

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־דָּתָ֣ן וַאֲבִירָ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ אַחֲרָ֖יו זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Moses, and he went to Dathan and Abiram, and went after him [the] elders of Israel.

en.L: And Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel went after him.
en.B: Then Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
en.R: Moses got up and went over to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel went with him.

decisions.choice: went to Dathan and Abiram: Moses goes to the men who refused to come
decisions.reason: Dathan and Abiram refused to come up to Moses (verses 12, 14), so he goes to them, with the elders as witnesses. The elders are the seventy who shared Moses' task (11:16, 24-25).

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־הָעֵדָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר ס֣וּרוּ נָ֡א מֵעַל֩ אָהֳלֵ֨י הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָֽרְשָׁעִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְאַֽל־תִּגְּע֖וּ בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם פֶּן־תִּסָּפ֖וּ בְּכָל־חַטֹּאתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, Turn away, please, from by [the] tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that [is] theirs, lest you be swept away in all their sins.

en.L: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, "Turn away, please, from beside the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that [is] theirs, lest you be swept away in all their sins."
en.B: He told the congregation, "Move away now from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away when they are punished for all their sins."
en.R: Moses said to the community, "Get away from the tents of these evil men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them. If you do, you will be destroyed along with them because of all their sins."

decisions.choice: do not touch anything of theirs: their goods share their guilt
decisions.reason: What belongs to the rebels is under the same judgment as they are and goes down with them (verses 30, 32-33). Anyone who touched it would share their fate, as with things devoted to destruction (Joshua 7:1, 24-25).

decisions.choice: be swept away in all their sins: share the punishment of their sins
decisions.reason: The word for sin also covers the punishment it brings. To be swept away "in" their sins is to be destroyed with them when they are punished (Genesis 19:15).

decisions.choice: when they are punished for / along with them because of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out that the danger is sharing the rebels' punishment, following meaning decision m2.

source.text: וַיֵּעָל֗וּ מֵעַ֧ל מִשְׁכַּן־קֹ֛רֶחדָּתָ֥ן וַאֲבִירָ֖ם מִסָּבִ֑יב וְדָתָ֨ן וַאֲבִירָ֜ם יָצְא֣וּ נִצָּבִ֗ים פֶּ֚תַח אָֽהֳלֵיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם וְטַפָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they got themselves up from by [the] dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, from round about; and Dathan and Abiram came out, standing [at the] entrance of their tents, and their wives and their sons and their little ones.

en.L: And they got themselves up from beside the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, from all around. And Dathan and Abiram came out [and were] standing at the entrance of their tents, and their wives and their {{gender:children|sons}} and their little ones.
en.B: So the people moved away from all around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrances of their tents, together with their wives, their {{gender:children|sons}}, and their little ones.
en.R: So the people moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the doors of their tents. Their wives and all their children, even the little ones, were with them.

decisions.choice: standing: taking their stand
decisions.reason: The verb means to station oneself, to take a firm position. Dathan and Abiram stand at their tents in open defiance, with their families around them.

decisions.choice: their wives, sons and little ones: the whole household shares the fate
decisions.reason: A man's household was bound up with him, and here it shares his end (verse 32). The sons of Korah, however, did not die (26:11); the Korahites later served at the temple, and several psalms bear their name (Psalm 42:1; 84:1).

decisions.choice: sons: children, set beside the little ones
decisions.reason: The word is "sons" but in a list of a household it can mean children of either sex; "little ones" names the youngest.

decisions.choice: all their children, even the little ones
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two words for children in one phrase.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ בְּזֹאת֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּן כִּֽי־יְהוָ֣ה שְׁלָחַ֔נִי לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּי־לֹ֖א מִלִּבִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses, By this you will know that Yahweh has sent me to do all these works, that not from my heart.

en.L: And Moses said, "By this you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has sent me to do all these works, that [it is] not from my [own] heart.
en.B: Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent me to do all these things, and that they were not my own idea.
en.R: Moses said, "Now you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent me to do all these things. You will know that I did not decide to do them on my own.

decisions.choice: not from my heart: not my own idea
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. Moses says that what he has done was the LORD's plan, not something he made up (compare 24:13).

decisions.choice: all these works: everything Moses has done as leader
decisions.reason: "Works" covers the whole of Moses' leadership challenged by the rebels: bringing Israel out of Egypt, giving the law, and appointing Aaron and his sons as priests.

source.text: אִם־כְּמ֤וֹת כָּל־הָֽאָדָם֙ יְמֻת֣וּן אֵ֔לֶּה וּפְקֻדַּת֙ כָּל־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם יִפָּקֵ֖ד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: If like [the] death of all humankind these die, and [the] visitation of all humankind is visited on them, not Yahweh has sent me.

en.L: If these [men] die like the death of all humankind, and the fate of all humankind is visited on them, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not sent me.
en.B: If these men die the way all people die, and only what comes to everyone comes to them, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not sent me.
en.R: If these men die a natural death, the way everyone dies, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not send me.

decisions.choice: the visitation of all humankind: the fate that comes to everyone
decisions.reason: The noun and verb come from a root meaning to attend to or deal with, often of God punishing. Here it means the common lot of all people, death in the ordinary course of life.

decisions.choice: a natural death, the way everyone dies
decisions.reason: Readable gives the two parallel phrases as one plain statement.

source.text: וְאִם־בְּרִיאָ֞ה יִבְרָ֣א יְהוָ֗ה וּפָצְתָ֨ה הָאֲדָמָ֤ה אֶת־פִּ֨יהָ֙ וּבָלְעָ֤ה אֹתָם֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָהֶ֔ם וְיָרְד֥וּ חַיִּ֖ים שְׁאֹ֑לָה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י נִֽאֲצ֛וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But if a creation creates Yahweh, and opens the ground its mouth and swallows them and all that [is] theirs, and they go down alive to Sheol, then you will know that have spurned these men Yahweh.

en.L: But if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} creates a creation, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and all that [is] theirs, and they go down alive to Sheol, then you will know that these men have spurned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: But if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does something entirely new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them along with everything they have, so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with contempt."
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may do something that has never happened before. The ground may open up like a mouth and swallow them and everything they own. If they go down alive into the grave, then you will know that these men have treated {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with contempt."

decisions.choice: creates a creation: does something new that only God can do
decisions.reason: The verb is used only with God as its subject, as in Genesis 1:1. With its noun it means a new and unheard-of act, something that has never happened (compare Exodus 34:10).

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead beneath the earth
decisions.reason: Sheol is the realm of the dead, pictured as deep under the ground, where all go when they die (Genesis 37:35). The rebels will go there alive, without dying first: their end will be unlike the common death of verse 29.

decisions.choice: spurned: treated with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to despise or reject with scorn. The LORD used it of the people who refused to enter the land (14:11, 23).

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

decisions.choice: does something entirely new / something that has never happened before
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "create a creation" means, following meaning decision m1.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֔וֹ לְדַבֵּ֕ר אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַתִּבָּקַ֥ע הָאֲדָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּחְתֵּיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as he finished speaking all these words, and split open the ground that [was] under them.

en.L: And it happened, as he finished speaking all these words, that the ground that [was] under them split open.
en.B: The moment he finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open.
en.R: As soon as Moses finished speaking, the ground under them broke open.

decisions.choice: as he finished speaking: at once
decisions.reason: The LORD acts the moment Moses stops speaking, which shows that Moses spoke for him (verse 28).

source.text: וַתִּפְתַּ֤ח הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶת־פִּ֔יהָ וַתִּבְלַ֥ע אֹתָ֖ם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְקֹ֔רַח וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הָרֲכֽוּשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And opened the earth its mouth and swallowed them and their households and all the people who [belonged] to Korah and all the property.

en.L: And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, and all the people who [belonged] to Korah, and all the property.
en.B: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, together with their households, all Korah's people, and all their possessions.
en.R: The earth opened like a mouth and swallowed them and their families. It swallowed all of Korah's people and everything they owned.

decisions.choice: all the people who belonged to Korah: his followers and household
decisions.reason: This means the people attached to Korah, his household and those who sided with him. It does not include his sons, who did not die (26:11). Korah himself was swallowed with Dathan and Abiram (26:10).

decisions.choice: the earth swallowed them: as it swallowed Egypt's army
decisions.reason: The Song of the Sea says of the Egyptians, "the earth swallowed them" (Exodus 15:12). Those who opposed the LORD's leaders meet the end of Israel's enemies. Deuteronomy 11:6 and Psalm 106:17 recall this event.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨רְד֜וּ הֵ֣ם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָהֶ֛ם חַיִּ֖ים שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַתְּכַ֤ס עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּאבְד֖וּ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הַקָּהָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went down they and all that [was] theirs alive to Sheol, and covered over them the earth, and they perished from [the] midst of the assembly.

en.L: And they went down, they and all that [was] theirs, alive to Sheol, and the earth covered over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
en.B: They went down alive into Sheol, they and all that was theirs. The earth closed over them, and they perished, gone from among the assembly.
en.R: So they went down alive into the grave, together with everything they owned. The ground closed over them, and they died and were gone from the assembly.

decisions.choice: went down alive to Sheol: Moses' words fulfilled
decisions.reason: The wording repeats Moses' words in verse 30, to show that what he said came true exactly. On Sheol, see verse 30.

decisions.choice: perished from the midst of the assembly: cut off from the people
decisions.reason: The men who claimed that the whole assembly was holy (verse 3) and set themselves against its leaders are removed from it.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: As in verse 30.

source.text: וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר סְבִיבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נָ֣סוּ לְקֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָֽמְר֔וּ פֶּן־תִּבְלָעֵ֖נוּ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel who [were] around them fled at their voice, for they said, Lest swallow us the earth!

en.L: And all Israel who [were] around them fled at their cry, for they said, "Lest the earth swallow us!"
en.B: All Israel around them fled at their cries, for they said, "The earth may swallow us too!"
en.R: All the people of Israel who were nearby heard their screams and ran away. They shouted, "The ground might swallow us too!"

decisions.choice: their voice: the cries of those being swallowed
decisions.reason: "Their voice" most likely means the screams of the rebels and their households as the earth took them. The people fled in fear of the same end.

decisions.choice: too
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "too", implied by the fear of the same fate.

source.text: וְאֵ֥שׁ יָצְאָ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וַתֹּ֗אכַל אֵ֣ת הַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּמָאתַ֨יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ מַקְרִיבֵ֖י הַקְּטֹֽרֶת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And fire came out from Yahweh and consumed the fifty and two hundred men bringing near the incense.

en.L: And fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
en.B: Then fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and devoured the 250 men who were offering incense.
en.R: Then fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and burned up the 250 men who were offering incense.

decisions.choice: fire came out from the LORD and consumed: the fate of Nadab and Abihu
decisions.reason: The words echo Leviticus 10:2, where fire came out from the LORD and consumed Aaron's sons for offering fire he had not commanded. The 250 men who claimed the priest's right to offer incense died the same way (compare 11:1).

decisions.choice: the 250 men offering incense: the test of verses 5-7 decided
decisions.reason: Moses said the LORD would show whom he had chosen to come near (verses 5, 7). The fire answers: not these men. The Hebrew chapter ends here; the story continues in 17:1-15 (numbered 16:36-50 in many Bibles), where their censers are hammered into a covering for the altar.
